title: wc_crypto2dev_cleanup() does not unregister devIds registered directly via wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice
description: The port comment (port.c:207-213) documents that wc_crypto2dev_cleanup() only unregisters devIds that went through wc_crypto2dev_register_ex() or wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid_ex(). If a caller uses wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice(MY_DEVID, wc_crypto2dev_cb, &my_cfg) directly (bypassing the port's registration helpers), cleanup will close the pool fds while MY_DEVID remains registered. Subsequent crypto ops on MY_DEVID will call the callback which will try to use closed pool fds, producing WC_HW_E. This is a caller contract violation, but the contract is only documented in a comment — not in the API header where callers look. The port.h header documents the safe functions but does not warn against direct wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice use.
